metadata.title: Gromov hyperbolicity and uniformity
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we first exhibit an example which answers negatively to a question posed by Herron et al. in 2008. That is, there is a rectifiably connected open set in a proper geodesic metric space so that it is Gromov hyperbolic with respect to the quasihyperbolic metric, and its Gromov boundary endowed with a visual metric is naturally bilipschitz equivalent to its metric boundary, but it is not uniform. Moreover, two positive answers are given under additional hypotheses. It is shown that a metric space is uniform if and only if it is Gromov hyperbolic and the natural map between its Gromov closure and its metric completion exists and satisfies a relatively quasisymmetric condition. Both bounded and unbounded cases are in our considerations via two different uniformization theorems developed recently by Bonk et al. and the first author, respectively. Finally, we characterize uniform metric spaces with uniformly perfect boundaries in terms of Gromov hyperbolicity and Teichmüller's displacement property.

metadata.title: Isosceles sets in Euclidean spaces of dimension nine to twenty-two
metadata.abstract: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erdős asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The answer was known for $d\le 8$, the last cases being due to Ionin. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le 21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre, and the number $\binom d2+3$ is attained. The proof combines Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets, for which we give a short self-contained proof (the key step is a special case of Gallai's theorem on edge colourings without rainbow triangles), with the recent determination of the maximum two-distance sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $9\le d\le22$ and with the known maximum sizes of spherical two-distance sets. In dimension nine this gives only $\mathrm{iso}(9)\le47$, and the exact value $46$ requires an additional argument about eight-dimensional two-distance sets with at least $44$ points. We also show that $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}$, where $g(23)$ is the largest size of a two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^{23}$, so that $278\le\mathrm{iso}(23)\le575$.

metadata.title: Logarithmically Slim Polygons
metadata.abstract: We study the relationship between the large-scale geometry of a geodesic metric space and the slimness of its geodesic polygons. We show that if there is a uniform constant $\delta$ such that every geodesic polygon in an unbounded geodesic metric space is $\delta$-slim, then the space has asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. We further consider graphs of bounded valency and allow the slimness constant of an $n$-gon to grow logarithmically with $n$. More precisely, under an explicit logarithmic bound on the slimness of geodesic $n$-gons, we prove that the graph has asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. Thus, sufficiently strong logarithmic control on the slimness of geodesic polygons forces one-dimensional large-scale geometry. We also obtain two criteria for graphs, outside the hyperbolic setting, to have asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension one. In particular, these criteria show that one-dimensional large-scale geometry can be detected from quantitative restrictions on the slimness of geodesic polygons, without requiring the space to be hyperbolic.

metadata.title: Filling Lipschitz spheres in metric spaces
metadata.abstract: We prove a homotopical Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Lipschitz maps from the unit n-sphere into metric spaces admitting a bounded bicombing, which includes CAT(0)-spaces and normed vector spaces. To do so, we first refine the second-named author's Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for singular Lipschitz chains to this setting. Then, we show that a singular Lipschitz chain filling induces a Lipschitz map filling of almost the same volume or less, by adapting a strategy seen in work of Gromov and others.

metadata.title: On Diameter Graphs Problems: A proof of Brass's Conjecture
metadata.abstract: The diameter graph of a finite set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ has vertex set $S$ and two points are adjacent when their distance equals $\operatorname{diam} S$. In this paper we study the following question: given $k$ and $d$, is there a constant $c=c(k,d)$ such that from every finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ one can remove at most $c$ points so that the subgraph of the diameter graph induced by the remaining points is $k$-colorable? Brass conjectured that such a constant exists for $d=3$ and $k=3$. We prove this conjecture by showing that at most one point needs to be removed. We also answer a question of Dol'nikov, showing that for every positive integer $m$, there exist a finite point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ in which every subset of smaller diameter has less than $(|S|-m)/2$ points.

metadata.title: Assouad--Nagata dimension of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals
metadata.abstract: We introduce the notion of systolic complexes with almost flat intervals. They constitute a subclass of fit systolic complexes and arise naturally in the study of graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes. We prove that their Assouad--Nagata dimension is bounded above by a universal constant. As consequences, we obtain universal bounds on the Assouad--Nagata dimension of tame simply connected graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation complexes and of finitely generated groups defined by graphical C(3)--T(6) small cancellation presentations. In the appendix, we observe that the proof of finiteness of asymptotic dimension for buildings due to Dymara and Schick also yields finiteness of their asymptotic Assouad--Nagata dimension.

metadata.title: Non-Pseudo-Arithmetic Hyperbolic 4-Manifolds
metadata.abstract: We give three explicit finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter lattices in dimension four whose adjoint trace fields are not totally real. They are the reflection groups of the Ma--Zheng polytopes $P_{11,6}$, $P_{11,7}$, $P_{11,8}$. The obstruction is contained in two cyclic products of the doubled unit-normal Gram matrix $A=2G$. Those products recover elements $s=\sqrt5$ and $u$ satisfying $$ (s-1)u^2+2(s-3)u+s-7=0. $$ After the embedding $s\mapsto-\sqrt5$, this quadratic has discriminant $8(1-\sqrt5)<0$. The cyclic-product field therefore has a complex place. Vinberg's identification of that field with the adjoint trace field and the Emery--Mila total-reality obstruction imply that the three lattices are not pseudo-arithmetic. Torsion-free orientation-preserving finite-index subgroups yield orientable noncompact finite-volume hyperbolic $4$-manifolds with the same obstruction. Exact computations check the census data and provide independent field and finite-volume certificates. A pinned Lean~4 development verifies the radical identity and the number-field obstruction. It also checks the lattice and manifold implications conditional on explicit geometric and literature hypotheses.

metadata.title: A sharp Bernstein theorem for affine maximal type surfaces
metadata.abstract: We investigate Bernstein theorem for the affine maximal type equation \begin{equation*} \sum_{i,j=1}^nf^{ij}(D^a)_{ij}=0,\qquad D=\det(f_{ij}),\qquad a\neq0, \end{equation*} under completeness of the Calabi metric. In dimension two, we prove that every smooth strictly convex solution on a convex domain is a quadratic polynomial whenever $a\notin[-\tfrac23,-\tfrac13]$, resolving a conjecture of Sun and Xu [25]. For every $n\geq2$, we also construct explicit non-quadratic Calabi complete solutions on convex domains for all $a\in[-\tfrac n{n+1},-\tfrac1{n+1}]$. These examples show that the rigidity range is sharp in dimension two.

metadata.title: Scaling Limits and Fractal Dimensions of $ω$-Substitution Graph Systems
metadata.abstract: This paper introduces a class of non-homogeneous self-similar constructions, called $\omega $-substitution graph system, in which the interface vertices are determined by an infinite sequence $\omega .$ The associated graph sequences naturally form compact metric measure spaces, and under suitable assumptions on $\omega$, we establish their convergence in the Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov sense. We determine the Hausdorff and box-counting dimensions of the limiting space. We further prove that the discrete Hausdorff dimension of the graph sequence coincides with the Hausdorff dimension of its scaling limit. As a direct application of the scaling limit, asymptotic formulas are derived for a class of generalized Wiener indices, which include the classical Wiener index and Kirchhoff index as special cases. Finally, closed-form expressions for these indices are also obtained.

metadata.abstract: A $\mathbb{Q}$-homology quadric is a smooth compact complex surface which has the same $\mathbb{Q}$-homology as a quadric surface, that is, the product of two $2$-dimensional spheres. metadata.title: Iterated minimal Darboux transformations
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the superposition of two minimal Darboux transformations in Euclidean three-space. A four-dimensional permutability diagram for transformations of isothermic surfaces yields the common minimal transform for distinct nonzero parameters and an explicit formula for its Gauss map. This formula determines the planar ends over regular umbilic-free points of the seed: an end is embedded when the two transformed Gauss maps coincide away from the seed value and has multiplicity 3 when all three values coincide. We illustrate this criterion with the Enneper surface and the catenoid. For the catenoid, suitable parameters give complete surfaces of finite total curvature, and we determine the numbers and multiplicities of their planar ends from the parameters and initial values. In the family with multiplicity-3 ends, the remaining initial-value parameter realizes, up to rotation, the López--Ros deformation.

metadata.title: Hadamard configurations and sharp cubic-period bounds for stealth in dimensions 10, 11, and 12
metadata.abstract: We construct explicit, nonlattice periodic point configurations in dimensions $10$, $11$ and $12$ with stealth center density $1/24$ and unit-density stealth radius $2\cdot24^{-1/n}$. These values exceed those of duals of the current record lattice packings, without claiming to exceed all possible lattices. The construction uses the $24$ sign rows of an order-$12$ Hadamard matrix and their antipodes, projected onto $n$ coordinates. For an arbitrary, not necessarily binary, equally weighted motif with marked period $2\mathbb{Z}^n$, we prove a sharp $2n$-point lower bound for a raw stealth radius at least one and classify equality by antipodal Hadamard configurations. We deduce bounded-complexity optimality, sharp optimality among binary motifs in dimensions $10$--$12$, and local maximality under simultaneous perturbations of the motif and the marked period shape. A divisibility argument excludes ordinary equally weighted periodic formal duals. Statements are confined to their indicated classes; no global optimality among arbitrary-period configurations is asserted.

metadata.title: Existence of Lagrangian Mean Curvature Flow Singularities with Bounded Mean Curvature
metadata.abstract: In every dimension $n \ge 3$, we show there exist Lagrangian mean curvature flows that develop neck pinch singularities such that the mean curvature remains uniformly bounded. This follows from a related result that, under a structural assumption on the singularity formation, the mean curvature at small scales near the singularity can be bounded by the Lagrangian angle at outer scales with suitable weights. Applying this result to a subset of the finite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed in the companion paper [ arXiv:2607.03152 ] and the infinite-time Lagrangian mean curvature flow singularities constructed by Tsai, Wood, and the second-named author [ arXiv:2401.02228 ] then gives examples of both finite-time and infinite-time singularity formation with uniformly bounded mean curvature.

metadata.title: Perfect Forms and Torsion Bounds in Algebraic $K$-Theory over Totally Real and CM Fields
metadata.abstract: We extend the method of Van Woerden \cite{woerden} to totally real and CM number fields to obtain an upper bound for the number of $\GLo-$equivalence classes of perfect forms. Moreover, by considering appropriate barycentric subdivisions of the Voronoi tessellation, we extend these estimates to the number of $\GLo$-orbits of $k$-dimensional faces of the Voronoi tessellation. As a consequence, we improve the asymptotic order of the bounds for the torsion part of $K_m(\rint)$ obtained by Soulé \cite{soule_hermitian_bounds} and Houriet \cite{Juliet_PHD}. We emphasise the improvement of the general bound for $F=\mathbb Q$, unchanged since Soulé's work, and the independence of the discriminant exponent from the field degree for totally real and CM fields.

metadata.title: A general Lê--Siersma formula
metadata.abstract: We consider the comparison between a Milnor fibre of a function $f$ and its section by the zero locus of a second function $s$ in a general ambient variety $\mathcal{X}$. metadata.abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.

Moreover, we establish a sharp Heintze-Karcher-type inequality for hypersurfaces in manifolds with a generalized substatic condition, together with its rigidity in Euclidean space with density.

metadata.title: On isotropic points and contact invariants of curves
metadata.abstract: Let $(C_{f},0) \subset (\mathbb{C}^{n},0)$ be a germ of an irreducible holomorphic curve, given implicity by $f(x)=0$ if $n=2$ and by $f(x)=g(x)=0$ if $n=3$, and parametrised by $\gamma:(\mathbb{C},0) \rightarrow (\mathbb{C}^{n},0)$. We define the contact invariants $\operatorname{Iso}_{f}$ and $\operatorname{Iso}_{\gamma}$ for $f$ and $\gamma$, respectively, which count the number of isotropic points that appear after a generic deformation of the curve. We first consider the case where the curve is regular and establish a relation between those invariants and the number of vertices, inflection points and the zero-torsion points (for $n=3)$ that emerge from the deformation of the curve. Furthermore, we consider a germ of a singular curve with an isolated singularity and relate the number of isotropic points with the Milnor number of $f$

metadata.title: Rigidity of Ricci solitons for $φ$-related metallic semi-Riemannian structures on para-Kenmotsu manifolds
metadata.abstract: In this paper, we investigate Ricci solitons in the para-Kenmotsu setting with respect to a $\varphi$-related metallic semi-Riemannian metric arising from the underlying almost paracontact metric structure, under the assumption that the potential vector field is pointwise collinear with the Reeb vector field. We first establish the relation $\tS=S+2n\beta\bigl(g-\eta\otimes\eta\bigr)$ between the Ricci tensors of the original metric $g$ and the $\varphi$-related metallic metric $\tg$. We then show that the Ricci soliton equation implies that the original metric $g$ is of $\eta$-Einstein type. By combining this condition with the contracted Bianchi identity, we obtain a rigidity result implying $f=0$, $\lambda=\frac{2n}{C}$, $S=-2ng$, and consequently $\tS=-\frac{2n}{C}\tg$. Thus, every Ricci soliton in this setting whose potential vector field is pointwise collinear with the Reeb vector field is necessarily trivial, and both $g$ and $\tg$ are Einstein. Finally, we provide two five-dimensional para-Kenmotsu examples: one realizing the resulting trivial Einstein Ricci soliton and another showing that failure of the required Einstein condition prevents the existence of such a soliton.

metadata.title: An ambient metric framework for sharp compactness of the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature problem
metadata.abstract: We develop a geometric method for studying $C^{2N}$-compactness of positive solutions to the constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature equation on closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds, for every integer $N\ge1$ and every dimension $n>2N$. Assuming the GJMS operator is invertible, its Green function is positive, and the positive mass condition holds, we establish sharp dimension ranges for the compactness of the set of all positive solutions with prescribed positive constant $Q_{2N}$-curvature. The largest dimension for compactness is $24$ for $N=1$ ([21]), $2N+20$ for $N=2,3$ ([11]), $2N+19$ for $N=4,5$, $2N+18$ for $N=6,7,8$, $2N+17$ for $9\le N\le17$, and $2N+16$ for all $N\ge18$. The constructions in [4,5,33,11] for $N=1,2,3$ and in the companion paper [12] for $N\ge4$ give noncompact examples in every dimension exceeding the corresponding compactness bound. We show that these $L^{\infty}$-unbounded examples can be chosen to satisfy the same operator and mass hypotheses, proving sharpness within this class. Our method relates the Pohozaev quadratic forms to the Hessian $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$, where $\mathscr{F}$ is the volume-normalized total $Q_{2N}$-curvature functional and $g_c$ is the standard round metric on $\mathbb{S}^n$. The ambient metric argument of [12] supplies an explicit formula for $D^2\mathscr{F}(g_c)$ on transverse-traceless tensors. The York decomposition projects metric perturbations onto this space. The scalar--vector--tensor decomposition represents the Pohozaev quadratic forms by explicit finite-dimensional matrices. We prove that these matrices are positive definite throughout the stated dimension range, a crucial step in establishing compactness.

metadata.title: Floer theory on based loops and fundamental groups of Lagrangians in $\mathbb{C}^n$
metadata.abstract: We obtain new constraints on the topology of Lagrangian submanifolds in the standard symplectic vector space $\mathbb{C}^n$ using Floer theory on the based loop space, generalizing a theorem of Fukaya-Irie. In particular, we show that non-trivial connected sums of closed, spin, aspherical manifolds of even dimensions do not admit Lagrangian embeddings into $\mathbb{C}^n$. A feature of the proof is that the obstructedness of the Floer theory is used to constrain the fundamental group of the Lagrangian.

metadata.title: The super Weil-Petersson asymptotic expansion and the coefficients
metadata.abstract: We determine the universal constant in the large-genus asymptotic expansion of super Weil-Petersson volumes. The argument adopts the uniform-transport strategy for shifted theta intersection numbers. The uniform large-genus theorem for normalized BGW numbers of Guo-Norbury-Yang-Zagier determines the amplitude at a simpler endpoint. The result is $C=\pi^{-9/2}$. We give a proof of the Griguolo-Papalini-Russo-Seminara conjecture for fixed boundary lengths and fixed descendant degrees. The boundary formula is uniform when the sum of the lengths is $o(\sqrt g)$, and we exhibit an obstruction at the $\sqrt g$ scale. We also compute the first four inverse-genus coefficients by two exact recursive methods and derive general polynomial structure results. Finally, we show that, for each fixed genus, the super Weil-Petersson volume divided by $n!$ is a polynomial in the number $n$ of marked points.

metadata.title: Perelman's entropy and Gromov-Hausdorff versus dynamical stability of round spheres
metadata.abstract: We study the Gromov-Hausdorff stability of round spheres under perturbations of Perelman's nu-entropy. We show that in dimension two almost maximal entropy, together with an area normalisation, implies Gromov-Hausdorff closeness to the round two-sphere. In contrast, in dimensions at least three, we construct smooth metrics on the sphere whose entropies converge to that of the round sphere, but which remain a definite Gromov-Hausdorff distance away from it. These metrics can be chosen conformal and uniformly bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the round metric, with the same volume as the round sphere. Finally, in dimension three, we contrast this Gromov-Hausdorff instability with a dynamical stability result: metrics with nu-entropy above that of the round shrinking cylinder converge exponentially fast to round metrics under the volume-normalised Ricci flow.

metadata.title: On the geometry of real polynomials of the 7-th degree with simple complex critical points
metadata.abstract: We consider real monic polynomials with simple complex critical points. Critical values of such polynomial $p$ can be considered as vertices of the uniquely defined polygon, symmetric with respect to the $x$-axis. The inverse image of this polygon is a tree-like system of ovals that touch each other externally in critical points. This system of ovals will be called the geometrical code of $p$. Let $a_1+i\cdot b_1,\ldots,a_n+i\cdot b_n$, $a_1<a_2<\ldots<a_n$ and $b_i>0$, $i=1,\ldots,n$, be the set of critical points of our polynomial $p$ in the upper halfplane, and $c_1+i\cdot d_1,\ldots,c_n+i\cdot d_n$ be their images. The order of numbers $c_k$ and the list of signs of numbers $d_k$ will be called the algebraic code of $p$. In our experimental work we study geometrical and algebraic codes of the 7-th degree polynomials and the relations between them.

metadata.title: 3-manifold decision problems and Riemann hypotheses
metadata.abstract: Beginning with Kuperberg's work on unknot recognition, several fundamental decision problems in 3-manifold topology have been shown to be in coNP assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis. In this note, we explain how recent developments around the quasi-Riemann hypothesis yield unconditional versions of these results, leading for example to the first unconditional proof that 3-sphere recognition is in coNP.

metadata.title: Chromatic Spherical and Renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev Invariants for Drinfeld Centers
metadata.abstract: We give invariants of pairs $(M,\Gamma)$ consisting of a closed connected oriented three-manifold and an oriented framed ribbon graph embedded in $M$ colored by a the Drinfeld center of a unimodular chromatic category $\mathcal C$. This invariant generalizes the chromatic spherical and renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants of three-manifolds. We use Heegaard-Graph diagrams which represent the pair $(M,\Gamma)$ and use the data of a unimodular chromatic category and objects of the Drinfeld center to construct the invariant. We define a ribbon graph associated to embedded framed links to obtain an invariant of pairs $(M,L)$. We show that if $L$ is the empty link, then the invariant recovers the chromatic spherical invariant, and if $M$ is the three-sphere, then the invariant recovers the renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant from the Drinfeld center. The relationship is proven by recovering a chromatic structure for the center induced by that from $\mathcal C$. The main theorem of the paper demonstrates that if the graph is a link $L$ colored by a generator in the Drinfeld center, then we recover the chromatic spherical invariant of the surgery manifold $M(L)$, contributing to a proof of the relationship between the chromatic spherical and renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants for unimodular chromatic categories, generalizing a recent result for unimodular Hopf algebras by Reina. To this end, we give a Heegaard diagram for $M(L)$ coming from the Heegaard-Link diagram representing the pair $(M,L)$.

metadata.title: Generalised Killing Spinors and Euclidean Hypersurfaces
metadata.abstract: We study when the number of spinors satisfying the same generalised Killing equation for a symmetric endomorphism field $W$ forces local realisation as a Euclidean hypersurface. Let $N=2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ be the rank of the complex spinor bundle. We show that in dimension $n\geq4$, if the complex dimension of the solution space exceeds $N/2$, then the metric and $W$ satisfy the Gauss--Codazzi equations. This is proved in the smooth category by combining the curvature defects into a single bivector and bounding the dimension of its kernel on spinors, using algebraic curvature symmetries to handle exceptional cases. Examples obtained from non-flat four-dimensional hyperkähler manifolds show that this threshold is sharp for every $n\geq4$. In dimension three, the Heisenberg group carries the maximal number of common solutions while failing the Euclidean Gauss equation. Further, in the real analytic category, we use existing extension theorems for Einstein metrics and parallel spinors to extend all common solutions to parallel spinors on a single local Ricci-flat ambient manifold. Using Wang's counts of parallel spinors, we obtain an independent proof of the sharp threshold for real analytic data.

metadata.title: Matching Random Point Sets with Minimum Distortion
metadata.abstract: How well can two independent random samples from a metric measure space be matched while preserving pairwise distances? Concretely, given two independent copies, each of $n$ points sampled from the space, what is their typical metric distortion as finite $n$-point metric spaces? We prove that the space $[0,1]$ equipped with the uniform measure already exhibits a rich behavior. We show that with high probability the distortion of the two independent samples is $n^{2/3}$ up to polylogarithmic factors. The lower bound reflects two competing obstructions. A bijection that maps points close to their original positions or their reflections in $[0,1]$ must expand the smallest gaps, in both directions. On the other hand, we show that large displacement from both the identity and reflection itself forces large distortion. Balancing these obstructions yields the lower-bound exponent $2/3$. For the upper bound, we construct a partial matching of the points that maps each gap between consecutive points of length $d\lesssim n^{-4/3}$ to a pair at distance $\widetilde{O}(dn^{1/3})$, with analogous control in the reverse direction. We then use a delicate multiscale oscillation construction to extend this partial matching to a low-distortion bijection.
